survey: An open treasure chest on a sandy seabed, seen in three-quarter view from slightly above. The front face (with a gold keyhole plate) and the right side face are visible. The front edges run gently down to the right and the side edges run back and up to the right, so the near corner is the front-right one. The box has gold corner trims and a gold rim, and its plank seams run along the front and side faces. The barrel-top lid is hinged at the back rim and tilted back. We see its curved outer top, the front strip with the clasp, the semicircular end panel on the right (in the plane of the box's right side), and part of the dark underside. The pile of coins inside is seen from above, and the coin tops are ellipses squashed to match that view. The gems sit among the coins. Outside, one coin lies flat as a narrow ellipse and another leans upright. The shell rests on the sand. The chest's base sits flat on the sand, which is drawn at a matching gentle angle.
